sections.html:
Whatcom County fills the northwest corner of Washington, with British Columbia to the north and the Strait of Georgia to the west. It spans 2,503 square miles and had 226,847 residents in the 2020 census. Bellingham is both the county seat and the largest city here. Blaine, Everson, Ferndale, Lynden, Nooksack and Sumas are the other incorporated cities, and the county also holds Lummi and Nooksack tribal lands, Birch Bay, Point Roberts, Sudden Valley and Geneva.

Two neighbors a few miles apart can pay different tax rates, because every parcel belongs to its own mix of city, school, fire and other districts.

sections.h2: Which Whatcom County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices matter to an owner, and each has its own job.

  • Assessor. Fixes every parcel's value on January 1 of the assessment year, using July 31 for new construction. Phone 360-778-5050. The same office runs the senior and disability exemption.
  • Treasurer. Bills and collects real and personal property tax, takes the real estate excise tax on sales, and runs tax foreclosure. The counter is on the courthouse first floor at 311 Grand Avenue, Suite 104, Bellingham, open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon. Phone 360-778-5160. Drop boxes are near the north rotunda entrance, outside the south entrance and outside the Treasurer's lobby.
  • Board of Equalization. Handles disputes over value. Three regular members and four alternates sit on it, all appointed by the County Council.

The Treasurer's website offers online payment, tax lookup and foreclosure auction notices.

The two halves fall on April 30 and October 31. Statements are mailed in February, and RCW 84.56.020 calls for a statement by March 15 when the budget and levy steps finish on time. A due date on a weekend counts as the following business day. Mailed checks are judged by the post office postmark, never a postage machine date, so on the due date ask the counter clerk to hand-cancel your envelope.

Tax payments are mailed to Whatcom County Treasurer, PO Box 34873, Seattle, WA 98124-1873. Use that box for tax only. Paying in halves is open to anyone whose total is $50 or more. A late first half is still accepted until October 31, with interest and any penalty figured on the whole year.

Late charges run on a fixed schedule:

  • A home of up to four units, manufactured homes too, is charged 9 percent interest a year and never a penalty.
  • Other property carries 12 percent interest, a 3 percent penalty on taxes still delinquent June 1 and another 8 percent on December 1.
  • Any delinquent year can be paid in full, with interest and penalty, without first paying the current year.
  • Foreclosure on real property starts when tax is three years delinquent, and the Treasurer holds a tax foreclosure auction each November.

Owners who live in the home and meet the income test can have leftover interest and penalties waived, just short of the three-year mark, once foreclosure is filed. The waiver is available one time per property.

No single rate covers the county. The Assessor's 2026 report sets a levy rate per $1,000 of assessed value for each taxing district, and your bill adds the districts over your parcel. To estimate a bill, divide assessed value by 1,000 and multiply by the combined rate. Here is a sample of 2026 rates:

Fire districts, ports and other districts add more where they serve a parcel. Countywide assessed value rose about 1.2 percent for 2026, and most of the increase in bills came from voter-approved measures instead of value growth. Staff physically inspect one-sixth of the county every year. Area 5, which included mid-Bellingham, Geneva and Sudden Valley, was inspected in 2026, and area 6 is next in 2027.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Whatcom County assessment?
sections.html:
Fill out the state form and send it to the county's equalization board. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due July 1 of the assessment year, or 30 days after the notice mailing, or up to 60 days where the county legislative authority adopted a longer period. The later date wins. Your Change of Value notice states the deadline that applies, so read it when it arrives.

The Board values property at 100 percent of market value and may lower, raise or keep your number. A late petition can be accepted for good cause such as serious illness, a natural disaster or postal delay. Appeals of a Board decision go to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. Before you file, talk with an appraiser at the Assessor's office, who can explain how your number was reached.

sections.h2: Tax relief for Whatcom County homeowners
sections.html:
Two programs matter most to owners under financial strain.

  • Senior and disability exemption. For 2026 taxes, the earlier qualifications still apply. A 2026 law change raises the income limit to $72,000 beginning with 2026 income, which affects 2027 taxes. It adds a standard deduction of $7,500 per person or $15,000 per couple, lowers the qualifying disability rating from 80 to 40 percent, and exempts participants from the state school levy in full. Three income levels, $54,000, $63,000 and $72,000, set how much assessed value is exempt from regular levies. Apply through the Assessor in person or online.
  • Destroyed property. After the December 2025 flooding, the Assessor lowered values on affected parcels in Sumas, Nooksack, Everson and Ferndale for the 2025/26 year. Values return to market for 2027 taxes. The Assessor's destroyed property coordinator handles claims for parcels still damaged.

Washington also runs a deferral program under chapter 84.38 RCW, and every tax statement must mention it. Ask the Assessor's office whether you qualify.

sections.h2: Taxes when you sell a Whatcom County house
sections.html:
Before the County Auditor records a deed, the Treasurer must receive a real estate excise tax affidavit and the payment, for every kind of transfer. An incomplete affidavit is rejected, and the staff cannot provide legal advice on filling it out. Interest and penalty start 30 days after the sale date. Have your escrow or title officer request a payoff from the Treasurer for any delinquent years and for the current half before closing day.

A gift transfer needs a supplemental statement signed by both parties, and a minimum filing fee applies when no tax is due. Mobile homes have extra steps: a mobile home that will be moved needs a tax certificate from the Assessor and an orange decal from the Treasurer. State rates and exemptions are on the Washington Department of Revenue real estate excise tax page and the county's excise tax page.

Pull these items together a few weeks ahead so escrow has what it needs.

  • Your parcel number and the latest statement, so the title officer can order the payoff.
  • Proof of which half you have paid, with receipts if you paid by mail.
  • The names of both parties for the excise tax affidavit, and the exemption reason if the sale is a gift or another exempt transfer.
  • Any exemption or deferral paperwork, so the Assessor can tell you what ends at sale.

Cash buyers usually close faster because there is no lender underwriting, but the Treasurer's payoff and the excise tax filing are the same either way.

faqs.q: What are the Whatcom County deadlines?
faqs.a: The first half is owed April 30 and the second October 31. A weekend due date slides forward, and the postmark from the post office, not the sender, sets the date on a mailed check.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Whatcom County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest starts after the due date, at 9 percent a year on a home of four or fewer units. Foreclosure begins once taxes are three years delinquent, with an auction each November. Income-qualified owners living in the home can ask about a waiver of interest and penalties.

faqs.q: How do I check what I owe in Whatcom County?
faqs.a: Use the Treasurer's online tax lookup or call 360-778-5160. Tax records are public. If you are selling, ask for the payoff for each delinquent year as well as the current year.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Whatcom County property value?
faqs.a: Yes. The board decides them. Look at your Change of Value notice. The cutoff is July 1 or the end of the notice period, 30 days or up to 60 if the county chose that, whichever lands later. The Assessor at 360-778-5050 can review the value with you first.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for excise tax on a Whatcom sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. The Treasurer collects it with an affidavit before the deed is recorded, and interest and penalty start 30 days after the sale date. Escrow normally takes it from the seller's proceeds.
